headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 6 studies yielded an effect size of 1.02 (95% CI: 0.95–1.1), indicating no statistically significant association between ultra-processed food intake and prostate cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential positive relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by moderate heterogeneity (I² = 38.15%), suggesting some variability in the results across studies.

Perhaps due to smaller sample sizes, those in the fourth quartile had a possible but non-significant increase of 31% (p=0.079).
